children: Mercedes-Benz
has beaten Elon Musk's Tesla
to be the first automaker to receive German regulatory ‌approval for its semi-autonomous driving software.
The German Federal Motor Transport Authority approved Mercedes'
assisted point-to-point driving system, MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO, based on UN Regulation R171 governing Driver Control Assistance Systems.
A harmonized regulatory framework for UN Regulation R171 is expected to enter into force in Jan. 2027, paving the way for the deployment of Mercedes'
software in other markets where the rules apply.
MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO will be available in Germany and the U.S. in the first half of 2027. Early access program starts at 2026-end in Stuttgart and Munich.
The software is a Level 2 automated driving system developed with Nvidia
, which requires active monitoring by a human behind the wheel.
Mercedes
and other automakers have been working with German regulators to get EU-wide certification for their self-driving systems, the
Financial Times
reported.
On the other hand, Tesla
sought regulatory approval for its self-driving technology from individual EU countries based on its U.S. certification.
Tesla
received approval for its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software in the Netherlands in April. Last week, Italy approved the software.
The company renamed FSD as "Tesla Assisted Driving" in Europe after regulatory concerns that the branding could mislead drivers, given that the system requires constant supervision.
Tesla Assisted Driving has received approval from 12 EU countries so far. It needs 15 countries to clear the software so that it can secure EU-wide approval through a vote expected next month.
China's Xpeng
, which is considered one of Tesla's
closest rivals when it comes to autonomous driving, plans to bring its advanced driver assistance system to European markets during the first quarter of 2027,
FT
reported.

title: Self-driving race: Mercedes wins German approval ahead of Tesla
